problem: Reported zero-shot ObjectNav gains of LLM/VLM pipelines such as InstructNav are confounded with detector noise and with geometry encoded in the stack, and one-at-a-time ablations leave these interdependencies hidden. It is unclear how much comes from language versus geometry.
motivation: Instruction-guided stacks (DCoN prompting, GLEE detector, VLM intuition map) are brittle, slow and costly, and errors propagate into the planner. The authors hypothesize that carefully engineered frontier geometry, not LLM intelligence, drives most of the gains, so they test this under a detector-controlled setting with ground-truth semantics.
key_idea: Replace InstructNav's LLM/VLM-driven action value map with a purely geometric frontier-proximity map (FPE) or with a light LFG-style LLM frontier vote (SHF), and show these match or beat the detector-controlled InstructNav at lower cost.
insight: Under matched (ground-truth) semantics, geometry-only FPE is at least as good as InstructNav-GT (HM3D SR 61.4 vs 60.6; MP3D SPL 24.5 vs 24.0) with zero API cost and about 2.3-2.5x lower runtime. InstructNav-GT produces an all-zero action value map in about 62% of steps, versus 28.6% (HM3D) and 36.9% (MP3D) for FPE, because DCoN prompts lack metric cues. With the noisy GLEE detector the ranking blurs, and reducing SHF's vote budget k to 1 slightly improves results, which suggests language is best used as a small local heuristic.
method: FPE (Frontier Proximity Explorer): removes DCoN and the Intuition map; the action value map is 1 minus the normalized distance to the nearest DBSCAN-clustered frontier point, within r=0.2 m; keeps the trajectory map, and the semantic map is used only for Approach/Stop.

SHF (Semantic-Heuristic Frontier): for each frontier, GPT-4.1 receives the object names near it and is polled with k=5 positive and k=5 negative prompts (LFG style, no coordinates); score alpha=(n+ - n- + k)/(2k) is spread within r=0.1 m of the frontier and summed, capped at 1.
Shared planner: target = argmax of the summed affordance map (action + trajectory), A* with cost 1-V_aff, switching to Approach and Stop when the goal is visible (as in InstructNav).
InstructNav-GT control: the published InstructNav pipeline with the GLEE detector replaced by Habitat's ground-truth semantic sensor, to remove perception noise.
LFG-in-pipeline ablation: LFG reimplemented in the same stack by dropping the trajectory map and using vote-based frontier scores.
Extra metrics: ASPL (action-based SPL, so turns count), API cost from the OpenAI dashboard, and wall-clock runtime.

setting.backbone: GPT-4.1 (frozen) for SHF votes and InstructNav-GT DCoN/Intuition; FPE uses no model
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D 640x480 plus pose, with the Habitat ground-truth semantic sensor
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: forward 0.20 m, turn left/right 30°, stop; 500-step cap; success within 0.25 m with the goal visible
setting.privileged: ground-truth semantic sensor for all main results; pose/depth mapping; the GLEE-detector ablation is on reduced splits only

numbers.extra: ground-truth semantic sensor; 500-step cap, 0.25 m success radius

numbers_note: The validation splits are called 'validation' in the paper; I mapped them to val-unseen. Reduced-split ablations (200 HM3D and 220 MP3D episodes, GLEE vs GT) exist in Tables 3-4 but are not listed. Baseline InstructNav-GT is HM3D 60.6/33.8/21.3 and MP3D 50.6/24.0/17.0 (SR/SPL/ASPL).
results: With ground-truth semantics, FPE reaches HM3D SR 61.4 / SPL 36.0 versus InstructNav-GT 60.6 / 33.8, and MP3D SPL 24.5 versus 24.0 (InstructNav-GT keeps the higher MP3D SR, 50.6 vs 48.0). It costs $0 and runs about 2.3-2.5x faster. SHF is comparable to InstructNav-GT and faster, but costs more in API spend ($366-424).
limitations: Main comparisons use ground-truth semantics, and with the GLEE detector there is no clear winner; FPE relies on a single detection to trigger Approach.
Simulation only, with no real-robot tests; the ablations use small reduced splits (200-220 episodes).
The published InstructNav baseline is not compared like-for-like (no GLEE row on full splits), and the baseline tables mix numbers from different papers and settings.
